topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the lecture and outlines the core learning objectives concerning the causes and mechanisms of cancer.

topics.label: Cancer as an Evolutionary Genetic Disease and Endogenous Mutational Drivers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental nature of cancer as a disease of clonal evolution driven by somatic mutations, endogenous cellular stress, and inherited genetic predispositions.

topics.label: Epidemiological Patterns and the Environmental vs. Bad Luck Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore population-level evidence for environmental cancer causation and address the controversy regarding the contribution of random chance versus extrinsic exposures.

topics.label: Biological and Chemical Carcinogens and Mechanisms of Tumor Initiation and Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific infectious, dietary, and chemical agents alongside the molecular pathways of metabolic activation, direct DNA damage, and chronic inflammatory promotion.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro techniques used to establish mutational signatures and evaluate whether substances cause cancer.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Everyday Risk-Benefit Decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This topic concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental risk factors and the practical risk-benefit decisions involved in managing cancer risk.
